clue.text: Dance right out of the drink bar

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: out of tells us a letter is taken away from the drink and bar run

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer leaves the bar of a pub to take to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R (right) from RUMBAR, the drink RUM followed by BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom step is a kind of dance.

clue.text: Reads here material to be recited

indicators.note: material here is read as the raw stuff that is worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor reads lines here, the material for a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' signals that the letters of READS HERE are reworked; 'to be' only links the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines practised aloud before a performance have been gone over, said again, recited.

clue.text: Divine food for many a girl

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Heavenly food enough to feed many a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman M for a thousand stands for 'many', a common crossword shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus the Israelites were fed in the wilderness by bread from heaven.

clue.text: How like a winter had the sonneteer's been

definitions.text: How like a winter had the sonneteer's been

parts.words: How like a winter had the sonneteer's been
parts.note: a misquotation-prompt from Shakespeare's Sonnet 97, whose opening line says how like a winter the poet's time away from his beloved has been

explanation.surface: A line of poetry asking how wintry the poet's spell has been.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver completes Shakespeare's Sonnet 97, 'How like a winter hath my absence been'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's separation from the beloved, his being away, is what felt like winter.

clue.text: This one was said to thunder

definitions.text: This one was said to thunder

parts.words: This one was said to thunder
parts.note: The Times was nicknamed the Thunderer for its forceful editorials, so a daily paper is the thing said to thunder

explanation.surface: Something that was reputed to roar like a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times, in which this puzzle appeared, was long nicknamed 'The Thunderer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a daily paper, famously dubbed the Thunderer.

clue.text: The dark part of Omar's Chequer-board

definitions.text: The dark part of Omar's Chequer-board

parts.words: The dark part of Omar's Chequer-board
parts.note: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam calls life a chequer-board of days and darkness, the black squares being the hours after sunset

explanation.surface: Asks about the black squares on the Persian poet's chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat says 'a Chequer-board of Nights and Days'; the dark squares are the night-time ones.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the board alternates days with hours of darkness, so the dark squares are the evening periods.

clue.text: An alarming creature for the timekeeper to track

parts.note: a watch keeps time
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: A creature that raises the alarm helps the timekeeper follow a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarming' is literal: this creature raises an alarm by barking at intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard dog barks to warn of intruders, so it is a creature that sounds the alarm.

clue.text: Uncle's visitor drinks a toast

definitions.meaning: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, whose customer pawns goods
one who pledges a health drinks a toast to someone

explanation.surface: A guest at an uncle's house raises a glass to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker; someone visiting one leaves goods in pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pawning goods gives them as security, and to pledge a person once meant to drink their health.

clue.text: A poor versifier, the sampler of " Ulalume "

parts.note: Ulalume is a poem by Edgar Allan Poe, so its author is meant
a taster samples food or drink

explanation.surface: A bad poet who has merely dipped into a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The author of 'Ulalume' is Edgar Allan Poe; 'of' places his name before the sampler.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of inferior verse is a would-be bard, a rhymester.

clue.text: Material for the artist over there

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
yon is an old word meaning over there

explanation.surface: Fabric for the painter standing over there.
explanation.walkthrough: RA = Royal Academician is a standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial silk is a fabric made from cellulose.

clue.text: Benefit of driving mirror? That's wisdom after the event

definitions.meaning: a rear-view mirror lets a driver see what is behind, giving a view backwards
understanding something only once it has happened

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the answer literally as rear vision; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A car mirror gives rear vision, and knowing better only once things are over is being wise in retrospect.

clue.text: Lament, for example, in Cambs city

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the name of the cathedral city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A sad song, for instance, heard in a Cambridgeshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambs is Cambridgeshire, an English county; ELY is its cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem for the dead is a lament.

clue.text: Contrary to the inclination of the cereal lover to be so

definitions.text: Contrary to the inclination of the cereal lover to be so

parts.words: Contrary to the inclination of the cereal lover to be so
parts.note: an idiom for going against one's natural bent, also read literally as someone who loves cereal being opposed to wheat or oats

explanation.surface: Someone who loves cereal would hardly be opposed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom from woodworking means contrary to natural inclination; read literally it would be odd for a cereal lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting across the fibres of wood, figuratively acting contrary to one's nature.

clue.text: Riddle for one examining evidence

definitions.meaning: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so the sense here is a sieve
someone who sorts through evidence carefully

explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is not a puzzle here but a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve separates particles, and an investigator sorts through facts in the same way.

clue.text: Sum paid to Peter for the freehold

parts.note: a fee is a sum paid for a service
Peter Simple is the title character of Captain Marryat's novel

explanation.surface: Money handed to a man named Peter to buy property outright.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Simple is the naive hero of Frederick Marryat's 1834 sea novel; 'to' links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, absolute ownership of land with no conditions is the freehold estate.

clue.text: A generous slice at the bakery entrance?

definitions.text: A generous slice at the bakery entrance?

parts.words: A generous slice at the bakery entrance?
parts.note: a very thick slice of bread is slang for the step at a front door, so the bakery's threshold is joked about

explanation.surface: A hefty slice of bread handed out at a baker's door.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a thick slab of bread is called by the name of the step outside a front door.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names a thick hunk of bread after the step at a house's front door.

clue.text: Growth of Mars for instance about a quarter

parts.note: Mars is an example of a planet
re means about or concerning
E for east is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An increase in Mars, say, by about a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' is a plant, not an increase; E (east) is one of the four compass quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall broad-leaved city tree is a plant, something that grows.

clue.text: Fault-finding may be decisive

definitions.meaning: inclined to censure or find fault

explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' simply links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorious people are judgemental, and a crucial moment is a turning point.

clue.text: O'Shaughnessy's music makers, Oxford spires

definitions.meaning: Arthur O'Shaughnessy's Ode begins 'We are the music makers, and we are the ... of dreams'
Matthew Arnold called Oxford's spires 'dreaming', so they are imagined as visionaries

explanation.walkthrough: Two literary allusions: O'Shaughnessy's 'Ode' and Arnold's 'that sweet city with her dreaming spires'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's music makers are visionaries of dreams, and Oxford's spires are proverbially lost in reverie.

clue.text: Mohammedan who calls to issue a summons

definitions.text: Mohammedan who calls to issue a summons

parts.words: Mohammedan who calls to issue a summons
parts.note: the official who calls Muslims to prayer from a minaret, read as if summoning someone to court

explanation.surface: A Muslim calling out to serve a court summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summons' suggests a legal writ, but this summons is the call to prayer from a mosque's tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosque official who proclaims the call to prayer summons the faithful five times a day.

clue.text: Satrap ran wild in the Peloponnese

indicators.note: running wild suggests the letters of the Persian governor's title scattering into a new order

explanation.surface: A Persian governor ran riot in southern Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran wild' rearranges SATRAP, a Persian provincial governor.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city-state of Laconia lay in the southern Greek peninsula.

clue.text: Piano unusually quaint, when sharp

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: unusually means the following word's letters appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A piano that is oddly charming, when played in a sharp key.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, soft) is followed by the anagram of QUAINT, signalled by 'unusually'; 'when' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent, tangy taste is sharp to the palate.

clue.text: Revised rate on railway, the bloody Tube

indicators.note: revised means the word rate is reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A revised fare on the railway, the wretched Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges RATE to TERA... ARTE, then RY (railway). 'bloody' sounds like a curse at the London Underground, but means carrying blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel taking blood from the heart is a tube for blood.

clue.text: To which Tommy's farewell was noted

definitions.text: To which Tommy's farewell was noted

parts.words: To which Tommy's farewell was noted
parts.note: the First World War soldiers' song It's a Long Way to Tipperary bids farewell to a West End square, set to music

explanation.surface: The place a British soldier famously bade goodbye to in song.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a British private soldier; the song goes 'Goodbye Piccadilly, farewell ...', and 'noted' means set to notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The marching song names this London West End square in its farewell line.

clue.text: Turner's articles in French and English

parts.note: la is a French definite article
the is the English definite article

explanation.surface: J M W Turner's articles written in French and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but here it is a woodturner, whose machine this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes work on a spinning machine, the turner's tool.

clue.text: Girl air pioneer grasps it in friendship

indicators.note: grasps means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Amy Johnson was a pioneering aviator

explanation.surface: A female pioneer pilot clutches something in a gesture of goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Johnson flew solo from England to Australia in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful goodwill between people or nations is friendship.

clue.text: Precious stone has page in revised " A to z"

indicators.note: in puts the page abbreviation inside the reworked letters
revised means the letters of the street atlas title are reordered

explanation.surface: A gem features on a page in a new edition of the London street guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges A TO Z to TOAZ, and 'in' puts P (page) inside it; 'has' links. The A to Z is a British street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow gemstone is a jewel, a precious stone.

clue.text: It wasn't Charlie with the straw hat

definitions.text: It wasn't Charlie with the straw hat

parts.words: It wasn't Charlie with the straw hat
parts.note: Bonnie Prince Charlie was the Young Pretender, but the straw-boatered French entertainer Maurice shares that title

explanation.surface: A man in a boater who was not Charlie Chaplin.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Edward Stuart was called the Young Chevalier; the singer Maurice Chevalier wore a straw boater.
explanation.definitionFit: The French music-hall star Maurice was famed for his straw boater, unlike the Stuart prince who held the title.

clue.text: Always ten? Really extraordinary!

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of the two words are arranged out of the ordinary

explanation.surface: Someone always scores ten out of ten, which is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges TEN plus REALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever, without end, is always.

clue.text: Growth of pronouns, possessive and otherwise

parts.note: thy is an archaic possessive pronoun
me is a pronoun that is not possessive

explanation.surface: Grammar lesson on how pronouns grow, possessive and not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' is a plant again; 'and' links the two pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant culinary herb is a plant, something that grows.
